walkthroughs.body_html:
IVF helps couples who struggle to conceive.

Step 1: FSH and LH injections stimulate the ovaries to mature several eggs. Step 2: eggs are collected and fertilised in a dish. Step 3: one or two healthy embryos are placed in the uterus.

Ethics: success rates can be low, it's expensive, and unused embryos raise tough questions.

Oral contraceptives use oestrogen and progesterone to inhibit FSH, so no egg matures.

In plants, auxin drives growth. Shoots bend towards light (positive phototropism) and roots grow down with gravity.

Auxins are used as weedkillers and in rooting powder to grow cuttings.

The body keeps levels stable using negative feedback.

Thyroxine: low thyroxine → pituitary releases TSH → thyroid makes more thyroxine → TSH falls again.

Adrenaline: released in fight-or-flight to boost heart rate and glucose; not under standard negative feedback — your brain switches it off when danger passes.

options: They kill sperm
They inhibit FSH so no egg matures
They block the uterus
They raise body temperature

mcqs.q: A shoot bends towards a light source. This is caused by uneven distribution.
options: Insulin
Auxin
Glucagon
FSH

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.
Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
